name: prlimit64
synopsis: int prlimit(pid_t pid, int resource, const struct rlimit *_Nullable new_limit, struct rlimit *_Nullable old_limit);
description: The prlimit() system call retrieves and sets resource limits for a specified process. It allows getting the current limits and optionally setting new ones, with soft and hard limits defined in the rlimit structure.

parameters.name: pid
parameters.description: The process ID of the target process for which limits are to be retrieved or set.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: The resource to get or set, such as RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_CPU.

parameters.name: new_limit
parameters.description: Pointer to a new rlimit structure to set, or NULL if not setting limits.

parameters.name: old_limit
parameters.description: Pointer to store the old rlimit structure, or NULL if not retrieving limits.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: A pointer argument points to a location outside the accessible address space.
The value specified in resource is not valid, or for setting limits, rlim->rlim_cur was greater than rlim->rlim_max.
An unprivileged process tried to raise the hard limit, or the caller lacked permission for the target process.
Could not find a process with the ID specified in pid.

examples: printf("Previous limits: soft=%jd; hard=%jd\n", (intmax_t) old.rlim_cur, (intmax_t) old.rlim_max);
